clue.text: Beetle moving like hare provides cover for tortoise

parts.note: the Volkswagen Beetle is a car
a hare runs fast, and apace means quickly

explanation.surface: An insect hurrying along like a hare somehow shelters a tortoise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' looks like an insect but is the Volkswagen car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell that protects a tortoise's back.

clue.text: Recover state separating blend

indicators.note: the state abbreviation splits the word for blend in two, sitting between its parts

parts.note: to coalesce is to blend or merge together
NV is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Nevada

explanation.surface: Getting better means keeping a nation's mixed parts apart.
explanation.walkthrough: NV is the postal abbreviation for Nevada; 'separating' says it splits the word for blend in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To convalesce is to regain health and strength after illness, i.e. to recover.

clue.text: Dogs soak end of nose in wet things

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it in water to soften it

indicators.note: the final letter of nose is placed inside the word for wet things

parts.note: rivers are wet things, a loose cryptic description

indicators.note: the last letter of nose is the one taken

explanation.surface: Dogs dunk the tips of their noses into puddles.
explanation.walkthrough: To ret flax is to soak it, a word met mostly in crosswords. 'in' puts E, from 'end of nose', inside the wet things.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrievers are a family of gun dogs bred to fetch shot game.

clue.text: Indicate reason

definitions.meaning: to ... at something is to indicate it
the ... of something is its purpose or reason

explanation.definitionFit: To point is to indicate; the point of an action is its reason or purpose.

clue.text: See 12
Talk about legend in one's puzzle!

indicators.note: the word for talk goes around the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: to jaw is to talk at length

indicators.note: the letter from legend sits inside the short form of one is

parts.note: one's read as one is, I + S
read as leg end, the last letter of leg

explanation.surface: Chat about some famous story in your brainteaser!
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'legend' as 'leg end', the letter G. 'in' puts it inside 'one's' read as 'one is', and 'about' wraps the word for talk round both.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture puzzle cut into interlocking pieces.

clue.text: 15's words from song, nuts to give up!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the letters are taken from inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A lyric from a song telling someone to abandon their crazy ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' hides GNUTSTOGI in 'song, nuts to give', and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a lyric and the title of a song recorded by Elvis Presley, the singer at 15.

clue.text: Worry cook

definitions.meaning: to fret or brood over something

explanation.definitionFit: Stew means both to fret anxiously and to simmer food slowly in liquid.

clue.text: Time spent in audition

indicators.note: audition means hearing, so the word for spent is taken as it sounds

parts.note: spent means exhausted, weak

explanation.surface: Someone spends a while at a tryout for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a tryout but means hearing: WEAK said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A week is a period of seven days, a unit of time.

clue.text: What sustains teachers? Nothing in France, student's conclusion

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
rien is French for nothing

indicators.note: the last letter of student is the one taken

explanation.surface: Asking what keeps teachers going, with nothing in France, and a student's ending.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a substance that nourishes, so it sustains a living thing.

clue.text: 15's moving 'ome first

parts.note: the title read as wordplay: love is zero, O, plus me gives 'ome, and the last word means moving; first says 'ome comes before it

explanation.surface: An Elvis song title described as shifting the home to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The title works as its own wordplay: love = O (zero) and me = ME make 'OME, followed by a word meaning 'moving'. Hence 'moving 'ome first' describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Love Me Tender is a 1956 ballad sung by Elvis Presley, the singer at 15.

clue.text: Giving up on that which is named Bond

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
a noun is the word that names a thing
cement bonds things together

explanation.surface: Abandoning the name of the spy Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' wants to be the spy, but it is the glue, CEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Renouncement is the act of renouncing, of formally giving something up.

clue.text: 15's silence so vital, or talents wasted?

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or wrecked, so these words' letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A singer wonders whether silence matters so much, or whether talents are being squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' rearranges all of 'silence so vital, or talents' into the four-word title. Silence is also what the title asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: A Little Less Conversation is a 1968 song recorded by Elvis Presley, the singer at 15.

clue.text: Such laughter in sitcom about a party detailed having moved holiday accommodation

indicators.note: the word for sitcom laughter goes around the rest

parts.note: sitcoms use recorded or canned laughter

indicators.note: de-tailed means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: Sitcom laughter about a lavish party turns into a holiday in a trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' means a party with its last letter cut off. 'about' has the sitcom laughter go round A and that cut word.
explanation.definitionFit: To caravan is to holiday in a caravan, a towed home, moving from place to place.

clue.text: Preliminary action result of overexposure

parts.note: a heat is a preliminary round of a race
a stroke is a single action, as in a stroke of a pen

explanation.surface: The early round of a contest, and a bad outcome from too much sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Heatstroke is the illness caused by too much exposure to the sun or heat.

clue.text: Temperature man loses extremes approaching Pole Star

indicators.note: the name drops its first and last letters

parts.note: Lord Kelvin gave his name to a temperature scale
S is short for South, a pole of the earth

explanation.surface: A temperature expert loses the ends and comes near the Pole Star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses extremes' cuts KELVIN to ELVI; 'approaching' just joins it to S. 'Pole Star' looks like one phrase but 'Star' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was a star singer, the theme of this puzzle.

clue.text: Amount put on, say, at a 3 unspecified

parts.note: some is an unspecified amount

indicators.note: say signals the word for put on is taken as it sounds

parts.note: to wear clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Adding some weight, perhaps, at a certain point.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is POINT, so the definition reads 'at a point unspecified'.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere means in or at some place or point not named.

clue.text: Lotus and pear used to produce seeds

indicators.note: used means worked over, so the letters of these two words are reorganised

explanation.surface: A lotus and a pear are used to make seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To sporulate is to form spores, the seed-like cells of fungi and ferns; a loose but fair fit.

clue.text: Order discovered in laboratory animal in feature which contains DNA

indicators.note: the rat and order go inside the facial feature

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: the order is found sitting inside the laboratory animal

parts.note: rats are used as laboratory animals
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An order is found inside a lab animal, in a feature involving DNA.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour. 'discovered in' puts it inside the lab rat, and the second 'in' puts that inside the facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromatin is the material of chromosomes, made of DNA and proteins.

clue.text: General concession

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ... was a US Civil War general

explanation.definitionFit: Grant was a US general; a grant is also an allowance or concession.

clue.text: 15's not great at acting vital part

parts.note: a stiff, flat actor is called wooden
the heart is a vital organ

explanation.surface: A singer is poor at acting but has a big heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden Heart was a 1960 hit for Elvis Presley, the singer at 15.

clue.text: Star sign's exclamation at lottery win

definitions.meaning: in astrology each zodiac sign has its own ...
in bingo, a game of numbers drawn by chance, players shout this word on a full card

explanation.definitionFit: A zodiac sign rules an astrological house; the word is also the shout of a bingo winner.

clue.text: Final note way over here!

parts.note: PS is a postscript, the note at the end of a letter
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A last-minute note with directions to come over here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final note' is a postscript, the note added at the end of a letter, not a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is a whisper used to catch someone's attention, like a call of over here.

clue.text: Priest with head missing — you can't tell who it was

definitions.text: you can't tell who it was

indicators.note: the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a canon is a member of a cathedral's clergy

explanation.surface: A headless priest leaves no clue who he was.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, used when the author is unknown.

clue.text: See 25
15's to suggest putting duck in red nest?

indicators.note: duck is a cricket score of nothing, the letter O, and it is added to the letters of the nest phrase

parts.note: the title read as an instruction: turn round the letters of its last two words and they give these two words plus the duck's letter

explanation.surface: An Elvis song title described as putting a duck back in a red nest.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is O, as a cricket score of nothing. Rearrange the last two words of the title and you get RED NEST with an O inside, so the title 'suggests' the clue's picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Return to Sender was a 1962 hit for Elvis Presley, the singer at 15.

clue.text: See 10
Person showing presence late morning or evening with flower

parts.note: at ten o'clock is late in the morning, or in the evening
a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Dee in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone turns up late in the day bearing a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is read as 'flow-er', a river: the Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendee is someone present at an event, showing presence there.
